sections.changelog:
Changed

  • **The results ceiling defaults to the full 1000.** The ranked pool was cut to 300 by default, which is where the "found" figure came from — so on a large catalogue a broad query reported the same count with a filter as without it, and the shopper concluded the filter had done nothing. Measured on a 13k-product catalogue: "экран iPhone 14" returns 651 matches, 552 of them in one category, and both figures were flattened to 300. Raising the default costs nothing in the search itself (the SQL aggregates every match either way, and LIMIT only trims the output), about 8 ms in the results query and 4 ms in the facet counters. Sites that saved their own ceiling keep it — the setting is at *Behaviour → Results page → Results ceiling*.

Fixed

  • **The category chosen before the search is shown as an active filter.** Picking a category in the search bar (or a category chip in the dropdown) narrows the results, but the results-page panel had no idea: it only ticked its own facet values, so the page looked exactly like an unfiltered one — same panel, same categories, and on a broad query the same "found" figure — while quietly holding results back. The chosen category is now the first, ticked value of its group, carrying the count of the pool it produced; unticking it lifts the narrowing, and "Reset" clears it along with the facets. A selector pointed at a taxonomy of its own — the setting accepts any hierarchical one — gets a group named after that taxonomy, so an applied narrowing is never invisible. It stays its own parameter rather than becoming a facet value: it narrows the search itself, before the ranked pool is cut to the ceiling, while a facet filters that pool afterwards — folding one into the other would have dropped every match beyond the ceiling (on the test catalogue, 300 products against 25).
